### 🏚️ Villages in the wilderness
- Abandoned settlements now stand in the generated world — farmsteads, sheds and larger buildings, laid out around a village centre and built on ground that gets flattened for them, so doors and floors sit where they should.
- What kind of village you find depends on the biome, and the forest thins out around one so you can actually spot it from a distance.
- Everything is generated from the world seed: your co-op partner walks into the same village you do, and a saved world rebuilds it exactly.

### 🏗️ Build your own buildings
- New **structure editor** in the main menu: build a single building with the map editor's own tools, save it to the online library, and it turns up in the map editor's palette for anyone to place.
- A saved building can also join the generated world — say which kinds of settlement may use it and how often, and villages start building yours next to the ones that ship with the game.
- The buildings that come with the game can be published into the library and reshaped: edit the farmhouse and every village in the world gets your version.
- The structure list in both editors is searchable, and each entry shows its size and how many pieces it is made of.
- Which buildings a world can contain is fixed when you start it and stored in the save, so a co-op guest sees the host's village and an old save rebuilds the village it always had.

### 📦 Storage crates
- The crates inside buildings are containers now, not one-shot loot: take what you want, leave the rest, and stow your own gear in them.
- Drag stacks between your backpack and the crate in either direction, or empty it in one click with "Take all".
- Crate contents are saved with the world, so a building you cleared out is a stash you can come back to.

### 🧰 Storage chests
- Craft a chest out of logs, sticks and scrap and place it wherever you want — 20 slots of storage, which is what stops the loop being "walk back to camp and throw things away".
- Aim at it, press E, and move stacks in and out with the same clicking and dragging as any other container. Its contents are saved with the world.
- The lid really opens and shuts, and two players rummaging in one chest both see it standing open.
- Recorded chest audio, cut so the thud lands on the frame the lid does.

### 🔥 The campfire is a place
- E at a fire now opens a panel and you pick what to put on: roast meat, burn a log to charcoal, smelt ore into scrap. Each click adds one more piece to the fire, so three clicks cook three steaks.
- Finished pieces stay on the fire until you come and collect them — start a batch, close the panel, go hunting, and your dinner is waiting when you get back.
- The progress card that used to sit in the middle of the screen for the whole batch is gone; the prompt just tells you when a fire has something ready.
- The fire itself was rebuilt: a ring of mismatched stones with one rolled out of it, bare earth and an ash bed inside, glowing coals, a tepee of firewood over a log burned through in the middle, spare wood lying beside it, and sparks drifting up out of the flames.

### ⛏️ Tools that do one job
- The axe fells trees, the pick breaks rock — neither works on the other material any more. A wrong-tool swing bounces off with a clang and the crosshair tells you it did nothing.
- Improvised edges like the knife still chew through wood slowly, but nothing except a pick opens stone.

### 🧭 Other changes
- Zombie headshots are worth 1.5× instead of 2.5×: aiming still pays, but body shots are no longer a punishment.
- Arrows now register exactly where they passed through a target, so an arrow can land a proper headshot.
- Arrows and grenades hit a turret's real body instead of sailing over the top of it.
- The trader stopped selling things you can already craft, and no longer sells ammunition at all — he deals in guns, gear and canned food, you make the bullets.
- The compass shows where your co-op teammates are.
- A crafting job's progress ring no longer replays from zero when you close and reopen the inventory mid-craft.
